Body scans, ref cams and football AI: Inside the World Cup’s new era
items.summary: The New York Times examines how AI is shaping the 2026 World Cup, from body-scanning analytics and AI-assisted refereeing to automated match-tracking systems. The piece discusses pilots underway, potential benefits in decision accuracy and broadcast experience, and the challenges around transparency, bias, and data privacy for players and officials.

items.title: SBJ Daily: Adobe, MLB expand AI tools; PGA Tour changes on the horizon
items.summary: Sports Business Journal reports on the growing adoption of AI across sports, including Adobe's and MLB's expanded AI-powered analytics and fan-engagement tools, and discusses implications for team operations, marketing, and monetization strategies.

items.title: AI disruption will challenge lending decisions in coming years - Goldman exec says
items.summary: A Goldman Sachs executive warned that artificial intelligence-driven models are reshaping risk assessment and lending decision-making, creating uncertainty for banks as they expand AI usage. The piece discusses how lenders must rethink credit-scoring, model governance, and the balance between automation and human oversight amid fast-paced AI deployment.

items.title: Citigroup raises AI capex and revenue forecasts amid rapid enterprise adoption
items.summary: Citigroup updated its AI spending and revenue outlook for 2026–2030, lifting global AI capex estimates to about 8.9 trillion and forecasting higher AI-driven revenue as large enterprises accelerate deployment. The bank cites strong momentum across industries and ongoing investments in hyperscalers and AI software.

items.title: Chinese banks boost loans to tech sector as Beijing ramps up AI push
items.summary: Beijing’s policy stance to accelerate AI adoption is driving Chinese banks to increase lending to tech firms and AI-related ventures, signaling a credit impulse to support domestic AI development and deployment.

items.title: PlaySight, Microsoft create generative AI analysis tool for pickleball
items.summary: PlaySight and Microsoft unveiled InSight AI, a generative AI analytics tool for pickleball designed to deliver advanced match analysis, coaching insights, and player performance suggestions in real time.

items.title: StubHub launches AI tool for rightsholders
items.summary: StubHub released the Distribution Manager, an AI-powered tool to automate ticket management for rights holders across sports and entertainment, streamlining ticket inventory and revenue operations.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher as traders return to AI stocks
items.summary: Wall Street rose on Monday as investors rotated into AI-related equities, with tech names leading the gains. The rally was driven by enthusiasm around artificial intelligence deployment and its impact on earnings prospects, with AI-related stocks contributing to a broader tech-led rebound and market optimism.

items.title: Analysts revise AI hyperscaler debt forecasts after Amazon bond sale
items.summary: Analysts raised expectations for AI hyperscaler debt issuance following Amazon's bond sale, with Bank of America increasing its 2026 debt forecast for hyperscalers to about $175 billion. The report underscores growing financing demand to support AI infrastructure and cloud-scale computing capacity.

items.title: IMF lifts 2026 global GDP forecast to 3.3% on AI investment
items.summary: The IMF raised its 2026 global GDP forecast to 3.3% on AI investment, signaling a broader macroeconomic benefit from AI adoption across sectors and regions.

items.title: FIFA and Lenovo unveil multiple AI-powered innovations ahead of FIFA World Cup 2026™
items.summary: FIFA and Lenovo unveil multiple AI-powered innovations ahead of FIFA World Cup 2026™ FIFA.com Media Release Fédération Internationale de Football Association FIFA Strasse 20, P.O Box 8044 Zurich, Switzerland, +41 (0) 43 222 7777 Wednesday 07 January 2026, 10:45 Organisation FIFA and Lenovo unveil multiple AI-powered innovations ahead of FIFA World Cup 2026™ Football AI Pro, AI-enabled 3D player avatars and next-generation Referee View revealed at Lenovo Tech World 2026 Group of “Football AI” innovations harness advanced AI to further enhance officiating technologies, as well as improve match analysis capabilities and drive fan engagement "Football AI” reflects FIFA’s strategic focus on digital innovation and AI, as outlined in its Strategic Objectives for the Global Game: 2023-2027 . FIFA’s Official Technology Partner for the FIFA World Cup 2026 and the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027™ , Lenovo provides AI-enabled devices, infrastructure, software, solutions and services at FIFA’s two flagship competitions and across world football’s governing body. A lead innovation for FIFA World Cup 2026 is Football AI Pro , a generative AI knowledge assistant developed to support all 48 participating teams in Canada, Mexico and the United States. The tool reflects a shared ambition to harness innovation not only to advance elite performance, but also to help level the playing field in an increasingly data-driven sport. At the highest level of the game, access to sophisticated analysis often depends on the financial and technical resources at a team’s disposal. Football AI Pro seeks to address this imbalance, with all of the 48 competing teams at global football’s premier event set to benefit from the same advanced pre- and post-match analytical capabilities. Powered by Lenovo’s full-stack AI capabilities and built on FIFA’s Football Language model, Football AI Pro analyses hundreds of millions of FIFA-owned and -organised football data points to generate validated insights in text, video, graphs and 3D visualisations. The interface will support prompts in many languages and will deliver consistent, tournament-wide intelligence based on millions of football data points per game. The new tool can be used before and after matches for match analysis, but not during live play. AI-enabled 3D player avatars represent a significant development in semi-automated offside technology. Players participating in the upcoming global showpiece will be digitally scanned to create a precise 3D model. Each scan takes approximately one second and captures highly accurate body-part dimensions, allowing the system to track players reliably during fast or obstructed movements. In addition, the 3D models will be incorporated into the host broadcast, enabling offside decisions determined by the video assistant referee (VAR) system to be displayed more realistically and in a more engaging way to fans at stadiums and to viewers around the world. The technology was successfully tested at last year’s FIFA Intercontinental Cup™ , with CR Flamengo and Pyramids FC players scanned ahead of their FIFA Challenger Cup showdown. The system was trialled throughout the match, demonstrating its capability and readiness to support the match officials at the FIFA World Cup 2026 . FIFA and Lenovo have also launched a new iteration of Referee View , building on the successful trial of the original version at last year’s inaugural FIFA Club World Cup™ . Using AI-powered stabilisation software, footage captured from the referee’s camera will be smoothed in real time, reducing motion blur caused by rapid movement. The stabilised footage will deliver a higher quality, first-person perspective for global audiences, enhancing transparency, understanding and engagement throughout the match. “The FIFA World Cup in 2026 is going to be the greatest show ever on planet Earth,” said FIFA President Gianni Infantino at the event. “Seven million people will attend the 104 matches – 104 Super Bowls – dozens of millions of fans will travel to North America to feel the FIFA World Cup vibe, six billion people will watch it from home, and the world will stand still. “FIFA and Lenovo are fully embracing digital technologies and Artificial Intelligence, “Football AI”, to support teams and match officials, while also providing a new mind-blowing experience to fans worldwide. With Football AI Pro, we will democratise access to data by providing the most complete set of football analytics to all competing teams and soon to fans as well. “The next generation of Referee View will show us new AI-enabled stabilised pictures to make the viewing experience unique – as if you are in the centre of the field with the players. “And AI-enabled 3D avatars will ensure precise player identification and tracking – a big advancement in semi-automated offside technology providing great images, faster decisions and a clear understanding by everyone. “But of course, this is just the beginning, so fans worldwide should stay tuned for more exciting developments with Football AI, and other innovations, as FIFA and Lenovo create unforgettable experiences in the months and years ahead.” Lenovo Chairman and CEO, Yuanqing Yang, added: “FIFA World Cup 2026, powered by Lenovo AI, will be most technologically advanced in history. We are providing complete IT solutions, enhancing the delivery and experience of the tournament at every level. Football AI Pro will be a gamechanger and we can’t wait to see it, as well as our other innovations developed with FIFA, used at FIFA World Cup 2026.”

items.title: Pacers Sports & Entertainment Launches Fieldhouse Media Network, Delivering First-Of-Its-Kind Global Media Channel for Partners
items.summary: Pacers Sports & Entertainment Launches Fieldhouse Media Network, Delivering First-Of-Its-Kind Global Media Channel for Partners | Indiana Pacers

items.title: Mistral AI Shifts Strategy Toward \"Sovereign AI\" and Agentic Systems in Asset Management
items.summary:
French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI told asset managers that the next phase of AI in finance will depend less on experimentation and more on control, as firms seek to deploy models at scale without compromising data ownership or compliance at the ALFI Global Asset Management Conference in Luxembourg on 24–25 March 2026. European companies are set to invest €150 billion in artificial intelligence over the next two years, yet most projects still fail to deliver value, Mistral AI told asset managers. Guillaume Bour, head of enterprise Europe at Mistral AI, said the gap reflects a structural problem rather than a lack of investment, arguing that many institutions are deploying AI without sufficient control over how systems operate inside core processes. 

The problem becomes acute as AI systems move into core business processes, where firms must be able to explain and justify how decisions are produced. Bour noted that \"Most models are black boxes today,\" which raises compliance and governance concerns for financial institutions. Mistral AI has structured its financial-services offer around three elements: sector-specific models trained with proprietary data, agentic systems capable of operating within defined processes, and infrastructure that allows firms to retain control over deployment. Bour described \"agentic AI\" as models able to take actions within workflows, such as know-your-customer (KYC) checks, anti-money laundering (AML), and time-series modeling for market forecasting.

items.title: UK FCA Issues 2026 Regulatory Priorities Mandating AI Governance and Accountability
items.summary:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has published its Regulatory Priorities Reports for 2026 for the Wholesale Markets and Wholesale Buy-Side sectors. The reports outline a pivot to a more outcomes-focused supervisory model, emphasizing the \"safe and responsible adoption of new technology.\" For 2026, the FCA explicitly expects firms to implement robust governance for emerging technologies by establishing clear accountability, risk management, and oversight for the use of AI and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT). 

Specifically, wholesale market participants must improve third-party and technology risk oversight through robust due diligence when integrating AI into trading controls and liquidity frameworks. For the Buy-Side, the FCA is focusing on strengthening governance frameworks to manage the firm's impact on markets, with a particular focus on effective risk management of investment models and strategies that employ AI. The regulator also announced that it will continue to collect information via surveys in Q2 2026 to understand the maturity of firms' insider risk management regarding AI-driven data.

items.title: US fourth-quarter productivity growth revised down, but trend remains solid
items.summary: WASHINGTON, March 24 (Reuters) - U.S. worker productivity growth slowed more than initially thought in the fourth quarter, but the trend remained solid, supporting the view that artificial intelligence and technology investment are still lifting underlying economic efficiency. Reuters reported that nonfarm productivity was revised down for the quarter, while economists said the broader trajectory continues to reflect business investment in digital tools and AI-enabled process improvements. The report matters for the AI-economy story because productivity is the main channel through which AI can raise output without equivalent increases in labor input, affecting wages, inflation pressure, and medium-term growth.

items.title: France's Mistral raises $830 million in debt for AI data centre build-up
items.summary: Europe's leading AI provider Mistral has raised $830 million in new debt to buy 13,800 Nvidia chips for a major data centre near Paris, according to Reuters. The financing underscores how AI is reshaping capital allocation, infrastructure investment and industrial policy in Europe. By funding domestic compute capacity rather than relying entirely on foreign cloud providers, the project highlights the economic stakes of sovereign AI infrastructure, including energy demand, supply-chain requirements and the buildup of regional digital-industrial capacity.

items.title: Anthropic to sign deal with Australia on AI safety and economic data tracking
items.summary: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would sign an agreement to share its economic index data with the Australian government to help track artificial intelligence's effects on jobs and the broader economy. The deal also includes cooperation on AI safety, according to Reuters search results and syndication listings. Australia currently has no specific AI legislation, and the agreement signals a concrete public-sector use of private AI economic-measurement tools for policymaking and labor-market monitoring.

Kirby Lee/USA TODAY NETWORK Teamworks has strengthened its position in elite football with the acquisition of Pro Football Focus’ enterprise data analytics platform. PFF’s consumer-facing business will remain distinct and will now license the foundational data metrics from Teamworks. Terms of the deal were not disclosed; PFF CEO Cris Collinsworth and the firm’s investors -- including Silver Lake and Western & Southern -- will become shareholders in Teamworks. Collinsworth is now also an advisor to Teamworks. PFF used LionTree Advisors LLC for the transaction. PFF provides football coaches and analysts unique insights and context, such as data labels on when the quarterback threw under pressure, what route the receiver ran and even what stance a pass rusher was in at the time of the snap. PFF is used by all 32 NFL teams and more than 240 NCAA Division I programs. It is Teamworks’ 14th acquisition and 10th in the last three years. Wide Left first reported last month on the prospect of PFF’s acquisition. Teamworks will now vertically integrate PFF data into the platforms of prior acquisitions such as Zelus Analytics , Telemetry Sports and Sportlogiq to better develop predictive models. “Having that PFF data definitely unlocks new possibilities for us,” Karim Kassam, VP/Teamworks Intelligence, told SBJ, noting that the combination of Next Gen Stats in the NFL and Sportlogiq’s computer vision tech at the college level means player tracking data is available at the elite levels of the sport. “The algorithms we use, the AI we use, it can do incredible things,” he added. “But to turn that player movement into insights that can actually be used by coaches and scouts requires football context, requires football knowledge at a very granular level, and PFF brings that uniquely in our space.” Teamworks works with 100% of the NFL, NHL and Premier League across its business units and more than 80% each of MLB, the NBA and MLS. The goal, Kassam said, is to create comprehensive data solutions for coaches and scouts in all sports. Football has been an early priority in the creation of that pipeline. “Having Telemetry and Sportlogiq and Zelus and PFF under the same house really makes data quality a lot easier because, when we get an issue, we’re not at the mercy of someone else to try and fix it or figure out what happened,” Kassam said. items.title: FactSet Launches AI-Native Banking Solution and Invests in Finster AI
items.summary:
FactSet (NYSE: FDS | NASDAQ: FDS), a global financial digital platform and enterprise solutions provider, today announced the alpha launch of FactSet AI for Banking, an AI-powered workflow automation ecosystem. Built in collaboration with Finster AI, FactSet’s AI solution for banking gives investment banking teams and, more broadly, research and sell-side firms, a unified, secure environment that automates complex deal processes and unlocks new data-driven insights. Concurrently, FactSet announced an investment in Finster AI, deepening its strategic commitment to next-generation innovation. This launch marks a bold move by FactSet to reimagine both the established market data and emerging AI agent landscapes, cementing FactSet’s leadership in AI-driven solutions for institutional finance. 
    
    “At FactSet, we envision a future in which powerful intelligence and AI agents seamlessly enhance one another; where, in an ever-evolving landscape, trust in core systems is more essential than ever as clients seek insights at pace,” said Kate Stepp, Chief AI Officer at FactSet. “With FactSet’s new AI solution for banking, we are delivering an agentic ecosystem that unlocks seamless access to an unprecedented array of datasets, proprietary agents, and task automation capabilities, all in direct support of our banking and research clients’ most critical goals.” 
    
    FactSet’s AI solution provides a unified, purpose-built workflow in regulated environments. Through natural language prompts, it orchestrates the production and synthesis of critical transaction assets and other complex processes across the entire deal lifecycle, delivering full traceability. The multiple agents within the solution streamline the proactive, trigger-based generation of pitch materials, company profiles, memos, deep research, and buyer/seller analysis. The solution is available through FactSet Workstation, with seamless integration into Microsoft Office Suite, and supports virtual private cloud or single-tenant deployment to meet the rigorous security requirements of the financial sector.

beyond a focus on fitness to also included broader wellness features. Courtesy of Whoop Whoop has added $575M in new funding at a $10.1B valuation as it reportedly eyes an IPO. Collaborative Fund led the Series G investment round with participation from more than a dozen institutions, highlighted by medical and pharmaceutical entities Abbott and the Mayo Clinic. Whoop has added a series of new health and medical-grade features and products in recent years, including blood biomarker analysis, an FDA-cleared ECG, insights on a user’s blood pressure and longevity-focused healthspan metrics. Lakers F LeBron James , famously one of Whoop’s first 100 users, invested for the first time along with other superstar athletes who made repeat investments such as Al Nassr F Cristiano Ronaldo and PGA Tour player Rory McIlroy . Whoop, which popularized the concepts of monitoring strain, sleep and recovery, gained attention at the Australian Open when the world’s top tennis players -- Aryna Sabalenka , Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner -- were all asked to remove the device . The app includes one of the industry’s first generative AI coaching tools . Whoop shared that it was cash-flow positive in 2025, its bookings doubled and that it has more than 2.5 million members; users receive the screenless tracking device for free and pay a monthly subscription fee, ranging from $199 to $359 per year. The Boston-based tech company recently announced plans to dramatically expand its staff from 800 employees to 1,400. Whoop founder & CEO Will Ahmed told Bloomberg , “This new raise allows us to really strengthen our balance sheet and ultimately invest more in areas of the business that are already working. We’ve had a very ambitious research and development road map that we’re going to continue to invest behind.” Bloomberg also noted Whoop’s international growth: four years ago, only 30% of users were outside the US, but that is now 60% of new sales. Notably, some of the Series G round investors include the Qatar Investment Authority, Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala Investment Company and 2PointZero Group, Australia’s Macquarie Capital and Switzerland’s B-Flexion. items.title: Anthropic Research Reveals "Implementation Saturation" and Productivity Barriers in AI Adoption
items.summary:
On April 7, 2026, Anthropic released a pivotal research report titled “Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence,” offering a data-driven look at how generative AI is currently interacting with the global workforce. Led by Anthropic’s head of economics, Peter McCrory, the study utilizes anonymized enterprise data from the Claude platform to distinguish between "theoretical exposure"—what AI could do—and "observed exposure"—what it is actually doing in the economy.

The report highlights a significant gap in adoption: while coding tasks have a 94% theoretical exposure, actual adoption currently sits at roughly 30%. McCrory describes a phenomenon of “implementation saturation,” where AI is rapidly taking over the execution phase of projects (such as writing code or running statistical models), but still requires intensive human "expert evaluation" to ensure quality and relevance. The research suggests that the highest productivity gains are currently concentrated among "power users" who possess the domain expertise to direct the AI effectively. Conversely, for workers without the ability to audit AI outputs, the technology may fail to deliver expected efficiencies. The study also identifies specific roles like microbiologists and real estate managers as examples where AI "reinforces" human expertise by automating administrative burdens while increasing the value of physical or interpersonal tasks that the models cannot replicate.

items.title: Bryson DeChambeau and Investors Acquire Sportsbox AI in Eight-Figure Deal
items.summary:
On April 7, 2026, an investor group spearheaded by professional golfer Bryson DeChambeau announced the acquisition of Sportsbox AI, a pioneer in kinematic AI technology and 3D motion capture for coaching and training. The deal, valued in the "eight-figure" range, signifies a major shift toward athlete-led ownership in the sports technology sector. Sportsbox AI utilizes proprietary computer vision algorithms to transform 2D video from a single mobile phone camera into a comprehensive 3D motion analysis, capturing precise body rotations and swing mechanics without the need for wearable sensors.

In conjunction with the acquisition, the group unveiled the Sportsbox AI Motion Intelligence (SAMI) AI Assistant. SAMI is an "agentic AI" tool powered by Google Cloud’s AI infrastructure that acts as a virtual coach. It can interpret natural language queries, provide real-time corrective feedback, and design personalized training regimens based on an athlete's 3D motion data. DeChambeau, a two-time U.S. Open champion known for his data-driven approach to golf, credited the technology with playing a pivotal role in his 2024 U.S. Open victory and stated that the acquisition aims to democratize high-level coaching through mobile-accessible AI.

items.title: Report: Regulated Data Involved in Over Half of GenAI Policy Violations in Finance
items.summary:
A new report released on April 9, 2026, by cybersecurity firm Netskope reveals that the financial services sector is struggling with significant data governance challenges as employees increasingly adopt generative AI (GenAI) tools. The study found that more than 50% of all data policy violations within financial institutions now involve "regulated data," including personally identifiable information (PII) and sensitive financial records. This trend underscores a growing tension between the drive for AI-enabled productivity and the strict compliance requirements of the finance industry.

The report details how "prompt injection" of sensitive data into public AI models has become a primary source of leakage, potentially exposing firms to severe regulatory penalties. As banks and insurance companies push toward "agentic AI" to handle customer-facing roles and internal auditing, the research emphasizes that current governance frameworks are often failing to keep pace. Analysts suggest that the high volume of violations involving regulated data will likely prompt stricter oversight from financial regulators, necessitating more robust, enterprise-controlled AI environments that can effectively "sanitize" inputs and outputs to protect proprietary and client data.

items.title: Goldman Sachs Study Finds 10-Year "Earnings Scar" for AI-Displaced Workers, With a Gen Z Twist
items.summary:
In a research note published on April 6, 2026, Goldman Sachs economists Pierfrancesco Mei and Jessica Rindels presented a sobering analysis of the long-term economic impact of technological displacement. Analyzing 40 years of individual-level data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the report identifies a significant "scarring effect": workers whose roles are eliminated by technology suffer real earnings growth that is 10 percentage points lower than their never-displaced peers over the following decade. The study finds that this is often due to "occupational downgrading," where displaced workers move into less-analytical, more routine roles because the market value of their specific skills has been permanently eroded.

The report provides a surprising counter-narrative regarding generational risk. Despite widespread anxiety about Gen Z entering an AI-dominated market, the data suggests that younger, college-educated workers are the most resilient. This demographic experiences cumulative earnings losses roughly half as large as older cohorts because they demonstrate greater "occupational mobility," quickly pivoting to roles that complement new technology rather than compete with it. However, the report warns that the timing of AI adoption is critical; displacements occurring during economic downturns result in significantly longer periods of unemployment and a 5% higher risk of permanent labor force exit. Goldman recommends targeted vocational retraining as a primary economic stabilizer, noting that participants in such programs see 10% lower return-to-unemployment rates.

items.title: Premier League Challenges UK Government Over Proposed AI Copyright Exemptions
items.summary:
The Premier League has officially lodged a protest with the UK government regarding proposed reforms to copyright laws that would grant artificial intelligence companies broader exemptions to use copyrighted content for training purposes. The league, which generates billions in revenue from domestic and international broadcasting rights, argues that the proposed "text and data mining" (TDM) exception fails to account for the unique value of live sports media and could allow AI firms to "scrape" match footage and data without providing compensation or seeking licenses.

The controversy centers on a policy "reset" by British ministers aimed at making the UK a global hub for AI development. The Premier League's leadership warned that such exemptions could undermine the commercial foundations of the sports industry by allowing AI models to generate high-fidelity simulations, automated highlights, or predictive analytics products that compete directly with the league’s own media offerings. This legal challenge is part of a growing tension between major sports rightsholders and the AI sector, as leagues seek to protect their intellectual property from being used to train generative AI systems that could eventually devalue live broadcasts.

items.title: Infosys and Carlos Alcaraz Partner to Launch Generative AI Performance Tools
items.summary: Infosys has announced a multi-year global partnership with seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz, appointing him as a brand ambassador to spearhead a new era of AI-driven tennis analytics. Beyond marketing, the collaboration focuses on the co-development of a generative AI-led "Performance Architect" toolset. This platform will utilize Infosys’s Topaz AI suite to analyze match footage and biometric data, providing Alcaraz’s coaching team with real-time strategic adjustments and predictive modeling for upcoming opponents. The partnership aims to democratize high-level coaching insights by eventually integrating these AI tools into the Infosys Tennis Platform, which serves fans and amateur players at major tournaments like Roland-Garros and the Australian Open. The initiative highlights a shift in the industry toward "athlete-centric AI," where professional players actively participate in training the models that analyze their unique physical and tactical profiles.

items.title: PwC 2026 AI Performance Study: 20% of Companies Capture 74% of AI Value
items.summary:
LONDON, 13 April 2026 – A small group of companies is pulling sharply ahead in the race to generate real financial returns from artificial intelligence, according to PwC’s new AI Performance study. The global study interviewed 1,217 senior executives, primarily at large, publicly listed companies across 25 sectors, asking them about the revenue and efficiency gains they are seeing from AI today.

It finds that nearly three‑quarters (74%) of AI’s economic value is captured by just one‑fifth (20%) of organisations, revealing a stark and widening divide between a small group of AI leaders and the majority of businesses still stuck in pilot mode. The research shows that these top‑performing companies are not simply deploying more AI tools. Instead, they are using AI as a catalyst for growth and business reinvention, particularly by pursuing new revenue opportunities created as industries converge, while building strong foundations around data, governance and trust.

Key findings include:
- Growth vs. Productivity
- Decision Automation
- Trust and Governance

The study warns that without a shift in approach, the performance gap between AI leaders and laggards is likely to widen further as leaders scale proven use cases and automate decisions safely.

items.title: Oracle Financial Services Extends Agentic AI Platform to Corporate Banking
items.summary:
Financial Services Summit, London—April 14, 2026: Oracle Financial Services is transforming corporate banking with new embedded AI capabilities and agents. With these advancements, financial institutions and corporate banks can now benefit from an enterprise-class suite of AI-infused applications and pre-built AI agents for treasury, trade finance, credit, and lending. These enhancements automate mission-critical processes and speed decision-making to help banks and their corporate clients navigate market volatility and risk, accelerate loan processing, and unlock new opportunities for enhanced growth and service. By enabling AI experience agents to engage directly with clients and bankers, and domain agents to collaborate across workflows, Oracle is helping corporate banks transition from fragmented, manual operations to a unified, real-time, data-driven system of intelligence that improves efficiency, compliance, and client experiences.

“Corporate banking runs on precision, resiliency, and trust,” said Sovan Shatpathy, senior vice president, product management and development, Oracle Financial Services. “Our AI-powered platform embeds intelligence directly into mission-critical processes, accelerating decisions and strengthening governance so banks can serve clients with greater speed and confidence.”

The new corporate banking capabilities are powered by Oracle’s next-generation banking platform that embeds AI experiences and decisioning at the core of every customer engagement and business process. Key corporate banking innovations include:
- Corporate Credit Loan Data Extraction Agent
- Financial Data Extraction Agent
- Loan Data Validation Agent
- Documents Data Extraction Agent
- Narrative Generation Agent
- Trade and Supply Chain Finance Application Validator Agent

These agents are a sampling of the hundreds of corporate and retail banking agents Oracle Financial Services plans to make available within the next 12 months.

items.title: Do VLMs Truly ”Read” Candlesticks? A Multi-Scale Benchmark for Visual Stock Price Forecasting
items.summary:
arXiv:2604.12659v1 [cs.LG] 14 Apr 2026
Do VLMs Truly ”Read” Candlesticks? A Multi-Scale Benchmark for Visual Stock Price Forecasting
Authors: Kaiqi Hu, Linda Xiao, Shiyue Xu, Ziyi Tang, Mingwen Liu

Abstract.
Vision–language models (VLMs) are increasingly applied to visual stock price forecasting, yet existing benchmarks inadequately evaluate their understanding of stock price in candlestick charts. First, prior studies fail to isolate VLMs’ comprehension of visual stock price inputs, and it remains unclear whether visual inputs genuinely improve predictive performance and whether VLMs truly comprehend candlestick patterns. Further, most existing datasets and evaluation setups are designed around single-period or tabular inputs. However, human analysts strongly rely on multi-scale candlestick charts, where longer-term horizons capture trend direction and shorter-term horizons provide cues for inflection points, making it difficult to systematically assess VLMs’ ability to integrate short-term and long-term visual market dynamics. To bridge this gap, we construct a multi-scale candlestick chart dataset and a standardized evaluation framework to assess VLMs’ ability to utilize multi-scale visual market signals. Evaluation combines confusion-matrix-based diagnostics with information coefficient (IC) time series metrics and includes XGBoost as a feature-based temporal baseline. Using this dataset, we benchmark representative VLMs and analyze their ability to leverage multi-scale stock price data. Experimental results show that most VLMs perform well only under persistent uptrend or downtrend conditions, while exhibiting weak predictive capability in more common market scenarios. We also identify significant prediction biases and limited sensitivity to explicitly specified forecast horizons in prompts, indicating inherent limitations in precise temporal reasoning.

Key paper details from the article:
- Introduces a new multi-scale candlestick benchmark using daily and weekly chart pairs.
- Dataset covers HS300 and S&P 500 constituents from 2015 to 2025.
- Total candlestick samples: 193,524.
- Evaluates major commercial VLMs plus XGBoost baseline.
- Finds most VLMs are weak in ordinary sideways markets and stronger only in persistent bull/bear conditions.
- Reports that Claude-sonnet-4-5(thinking) shows strong predictive power in both direction and ranking; Gemini2.5-pro on S&P 500 achieves top IC and Rank IC means in the reported table.
- Concludes current VLMs appear more useful as short-term signal aids than robust long-horizon forecasting systems.

items.title: Research: AI Exposure Linked to Job and Wage Growth in Efficient Labor Markets
items.summary:
In a new research paper, labor economist Christos Makridis (ASU) and Andrew Johnston analyze how exposure to generative AI affected U.S. industries between 2017 and 2024. Using administrative data covering nearly all employers, the researchers measured AI exposure based on occupation-level task data, comparing industries with high language-processing and data-task requirements against those with physical labor requirements.

The study found that industries most exposed to AI experienced faster productivity growth beginning in 2021, driven by enterprise tools like GitHub Copilot and Jasper. By 2024, industries with AI exposure one standard deviation higher saw productivity gains of 10%, a 3.9% increase in jobs, and 4.8% higher wage growth compared to peers.

Key differentiators identified:
- Augmentation vs. Displacement
- Economic Output
- Organizational Trust

The findings suggest that AI is currently acting as a productivity-enhancing tool that boosts overall demand for labor by lowering the cost of tasks and expanding business output, provided labor markets are efficient and management creates safe environments for experimentation.

items.title: Banks rush for access to Anthropic’s Mythos as regulators flag rising cybersecurity risks
items.summary:
Major global financial institutions, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup, have begun internal testing of Anthropic’s latest AI model, "Mythos." The model, developed under the restricted "Project Glasswing" initiative, has drawn intense interest for its advanced reasoning and coding capabilities. However, its deployment has triggered a wave of regulatory concern regarding its potential for "cyber offence."

The UK government issued a formal warning on April 15, 2026, stating that testing showed Mythos is substantially more capable of executing cyberattacks than previous models, posing a direct threat to banks reliant on legacy infrastructure. On the sidelines of the IMF Spring Meetings, executives from Deutsche Bank and Barclays described the model as a "serious risk to the global banking system" if not strictly governed. Regulators in South Korea and the European Central Bank (ECB) have initiated "quiz" sessions with bank leadership to evaluate their preparedness for AI-supercharged threats. Despite these risks, banks are racing for access to avoid a perceived competitive disadvantage in automated software development and risk modeling.

items.title: Lloyds pilots AI investment guidance tool as UK regulator studies impact
items.summary:
Lloyds Banking Group has officially become the first major UK lender to deploy a generative AI-powered "investment guidance" tool for retail customers. The pilot program, launched on April 21, 2026, aims to bridge the "advice gap" by providing personalized portfolio suggestions and market education to customers who do not meet the high-net-worth thresholds for traditional human financial advisors.

The tool utilizes a proprietary large language model (LLM) to analyze customer risk profiles and financial goals, offering real-time explanations for specific asset allocations. The launch coincides with a thematic review by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), which is closely monitoring the deployment to ensure the AI does not cross the boundary into "unregulated advice" or display harmful biases. Lloyds’ initiative is seen as a test case for the industry’s ability to use AI for mass-market wealth management while adhering to the UK’s strict "Consumer Duty" regulations.

items.title: Amazon broadcast details: Prime Vision, Rapid Recap, more features on platform's first NBA playoffs coverage
items.summary:
Amazon Prime Video has launched its first-ever NBA playoff coverage (beginning April 18, 2026) following a landmark media rights deal. Central to the broadcast is "Prime Vision," an AI-enhanced viewing mode that provides real-time tactical overlays. The AI model analyzes player positioning to identify mismatches—such as a size advantage or a defensive lapse—and highlights them for viewers using on-screen graphic circles.

In addition to live tactical analysis, the platform utilizes AWS-powered advanced statistics to provide "Rapid Recap" and "Key Moments" features. These tools use machine learning to automatically curate highlight reels, bringing late-arriving fans up to speed by identifying the most significant plays based on momentum shifts and scoring impact. The broadcast also integrates personalized bet tracking via FanDuel, further demonstrating how AI is being used to create a more interactive and data-rich "second-screen" experience for sports fans.

items.title: Dissecting AI Trading: Behavioral Finance and Market Bubbles
items.summary:
Dissecting AI Trading: Behavioral Finance and Market Bubbles  
Authors: Shumiao Ouyang (Saïd Business School, University of Oxford), Pengfei Sui (Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen)  

**Abstract**  
We study how AI agents form expectations and trade in experimental asset markets. Using a simulated open-call auction populated by autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents, we document three main findings. First, AI agents exhibit classic behavioral patterns: a pronounced disposition effect and recency-weighted extrapolative beliefs. Second, these individual-level patterns aggregate into equilibrium dynamics that replicate classic experimental findings, including the predictive power of excess demand for future prices and the positive relationship between disagreement and trading volume. Third, by analyzing the agents’ reasoning text through a twenty-mechanism scoring framework, we show that targeted prompt interventions causally amplify or suppress specific behavioral mechanisms, significantly altering the magnitude of market bubbles.

**Key details from the paper**  
- Submitted on 2026-04-20.  
- Simulates a full asset market using autonomous LLM traders in an open-call auction setting.  
- Finds AI traders reproduce classic human finance biases, including the disposition effect and extrapolative expectations.  
- Shows these micro-level biases aggregate into macro-level bubble dynamics and predictable volume/disagreement relationships.  
- Demonstrates that prompt-based “cognitive guardrails” can reduce bubble magnitude, suggesting a practical control lever for AI-driven financial markets.  
- Strong relevance for algorithmic trading, financial stability, and AI-agent governance in markets.

items.title: Thousands of CEOs admit AI had no impact on employment or productivity—and it has economists resurrecting a paradox from 40 years ago
items.summary:
In 1987, economist and Nobel laureate Robert Solow made a stark observation about the stalling evolution of the Information Age: Following the advent of transistors, microprocessors, integrated circuits, and memory chips of the 1960s, economists and companies expected these new technologies to disrupt workplaces and result in a surge of productivity. Instead, productivity growth slowed, dropping from 2.9% from 1948 to 1973, to 1.1% after 1973. This unexpected outcome became known as Solow’s productivity paradox. “You can see the computer age everywhere but in the productivity statistics,” Solow wrote.

Data on how C-suite executives are—or aren’t—using AI shows history is repeating itself. Despite 374 companies in the S&P 500 mentioning AI in earnings calls, a study published by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) found that among 6,000 CEOs and CFOs in the U.S., U.K., Germany, and Australia, the vast majority see little impact from AI on their operations. Nearly 90% of firms said AI has had no impact on employment or productivity over the past three years. While about two-thirds of executives reported using AI, that usage amounted to only about 1.5 hours per week.

However, firms’ expectations remain substantial: Executives forecast AI will increase productivity by 1.4% and output by 0.8% over the next three years. Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok invoked Solow’s observation, noting that "AI is everywhere except in the incoming macroeconomic data." Slok suggested the future impact might resemble a “J-curve”—an initial slowdown in performance followed by an exponential surge, depending on how AI is implemented across different sectors rather than the mere existence of the technology itself.
